what_its_for: Pemigatinib is a cancer medicine used to treat adults with a type of bile duct cancer called cholangiocarcinoma that has spread or cannot be removed by surgery. It works in patients whose cancer has a specific gene change (called FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement). It may also be used for certain other cancers with FGFR gene changes. Your doctor will test your tumor to make sure this medicine is right for you.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with or without food. Do not crush, cut, or chew the tablet. Take it at the same time each day. If you vomit after taking your dose, do not take an extra dose — just take your next scheduled dose at the regular time.
dosing: The usual dose is 13.5 mg taken once a day for 14 days in a row, followed by 7 days off (no medicine). This 21-day cycle is then repeated. Your doctor may lower your dose or temporarily stop your medicine if you have side effects. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been less than 4 hours since your scheduled time, take it as soon as you remember. If it has been more than 4 hours, skip that missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep this medicine away from moisture, heat, and direct light. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of any unused or expired tablets safely — ask your pharmacist about medicine take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Avoid foods and drinks that contain grapefruit or Seville oranges (used in some marmalades), as they can increase the amount of this medicine in your body and make side effects worse. Avoid becoming pregnant while taking this medicine, as it can harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 1 week after your last dose. Tell your doctor about ALL other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, because many drugs can interact with pemigatinib, including certain antifungals, antibiotics, and seizure medicines.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you notice: serious eye problems such as sudden vision changes, blurred vision, dry or painful eyes, or light sensitivity (these may be signs of a condition called central serous retinopathy); signs of high phosphate levels in your blood such as muscle cramps, joint pain, or unusual tiredness; signs of low phosphate levels such as weakness, bone pain, or confusion; unusual bone pain or fractures; signs of skin problems such as severe rash, peeling, or blistering; signs of infection such as fever or chills; unusual swelling or weight gain; or any new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: It may take several weeks before your doctor can tell if the medicine is working. Your doctor will check your progress with regular blood tests and imaging scans (such as CT scans or MRIs). Do not stop taking the medicine unless your doctor tells you to, even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do not use if you are pregnant. This medicine can cause harm or loss of a pregnancy. Women who can become pregnant should use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 1 week after the last dose. Men with female partners who can become pregnant should also use birth control during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine and for at least 1 week after the last dose. Liver or kidney problems: Your doctor may adjust your dose if you have moderate-to-severe liver problems. Tell your doctor about any kidney or liver conditions you have. Older adults: Older patients can take this medicine, but may need extra monitoring for side effects.
